verdict: Cigna grew revenue 6% to $73.7B on pharmacy and premium growth, but shareholders' profit fell to $1.4B from $1.9B, largely because last year's quarter included a gain on a business sale.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted shareholders' EPS, vs $6.98 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $7.98

kpis.label: Medical care ratio
kpis.note: share of Cigna Healthcare premiums paid out as medical costs, vs 84.8% a year ago

segments.name: Pharmacy revenues
segments.note: Drugs dispensed and pharmacy services, mainly through Evernorth — pharmacy benefit services and specialty pharmacy. This is the money that flows through Cigna to pay for medicines, up 5%.

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums paid by members, employers and government programs for Cigna Healthcare coverage — up 9%.

segments.name: Fees and other revenues
segments.note: Fees for administering health plans and other services, plus other smaller revenue — up 3%.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio — up 23%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — people, technology and offices. At 4.9% of revenue, the SG&A ratio edged up from 4.8% as the company invested for growth.

opex.name: Amortization of acquired intangibles
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of businesses Cigna bought in earlier deals over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $297M: $333M of interest expense and other costs, partly offset by $36M of net investment gains. Net investment income of $287M is already counted in revenue, not in this line.
oneTimers: Adjusted income from operations of $2,104M excludes special items booked in the quarter — an $85M strategic optimization (modernization) charge, $60M of litigation charges and $23M of integration and transaction costs, all pre-tax — as well as the $589M amortization of acquired intangibles and net investment losses.

A year ago, shareholders' net income was lifted by an after-tax gain on the sale of businesses; there was no such gain this quarter, which is the main reason GAAP profit fell even though adjusted profit was flat.
footerNote: Following the managed-care model: pharmacy and medical costs are the direct-cost block. Consolidated net income was $1,698M; after $256M attributable to noncontrolling interests, shareholders' net income was $1,442M ($5.47 per diluted share).

takeaways.title: Growth in both halves
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 6% to $73,683M, driven by both Evernorth Health Services and Cigna Healthcare. Evernorth's adjusted revenues were $63,774M — pharmacy benefit services $37,276M and specialty and care services $26,498M.

takeaways.title: Medical costs held steady
takeaways.text: Cigna Healthcare's medical care ratio — medical costs as a share of premiums — was 85.0%, close to 84.8% a year ago, and the segment's adjusted operating income rose 15%. Medical customers grew to 18.5M, up 2% from year-end.

takeaways.title: Full-year outlook raised
takeaways.text: Cigna raised its 2026 outlook for adjusted income from operations to at least $30.60 per share, and narrowed its expected medical care ratio to 84.2% plus or minus 0.25 points. GAAP EPS of $5.47 compares with adjusted EPS of $7.98 — the gap is mainly amortization and special items.
